3. The defendant appeared in the suit land filed a written statement stating that the deed of gilt was valid and there was an exchange or ewaj. He also stated that the suit is barred by limitation. 

 4. The trial court upon hearing the parties and also considering the evidence on record found that the plaintiff petitioner is an illiterate village woman and the transaction of the heba bil ewaj was not proved and no exchange was passed and the suit was not barred by limitation as such decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 15.5.93. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendant-opposite party filed Title Appeal No. 177/93 before the District Judge and the same was disposed 'of by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court; Barisal. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court on the finding that the plaintiff did not pay ad-valorem court fee and the suit is barred by limitation as the suit was not filed within 6 years from the date of knowledge and further the plaintiff failed to prove that the document is a genuine one. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree the petitioner filed this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in setting aside the decree of the Trial Court. He has not controverted the finding of the fact arrived at by the trial court and illegally allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and decree of the Trial Court. 

 5. Heard the learned Advocates, perused the application and also the judgments of the Courts below. Both the courts found that the suit property originally belonged to the plaintiff—petitioner. The trial court found that on 25.10.72 the petitioner's pardahnashin village woman went to the Sub-Registrar office with a view to selling out 15 decimals of land in favour of one Abdul Jabbar Howlader and Abdul Kader but her sons by the first husband and her brother Kashem Ali upon practicing fraud get the heba bil ewaj executed and registered. On the first part of 1390 B.S. the defendant for the first time claimed the land and the plaintiff Searched before the Sub-Registry office and found that a collusive forged heba bil ewaj was created. It is stated that the petitioner had been in possession although. It is further stated that she did not go to the Sub-Registry  office and did never execute and register any heba bil ewaj as such she filed the suit for a declaration that the heba bil ewaj is a false, fraudulent, collusive document which is not binding upon the plaintiff petitioner. The plaintiff admitted that the signature appearing in the heba bil ewaj was her signature but she asserted that she put her signature to sell out the land in favour of one Abdul Jabbar Howlader and Abdul Kader but her sons by the first husband and her brother Kashem Ali by practising fraud used the stamp paper for creating the heba bil ewaj without the knowledge of the plaintiff-petitioner. She did never .execute or register the heba bil ewaj and it was never known to her. The learned Subordinate Judge found that all the 3 witnesses in the heba bil ewaj including the scribed are the persons of the Sub-Registrar office and in collusion with each other they created the heba bil ewaj. All the D.Ws. stated about the exchange of Jainamaj and Tosbi which is disbelieved by the trial court. The Court also found that the defendant failed to prove their possession and he found that the plaintiff had been in possession of the suit land although and the possession of the defendant could not be established. As the possession was not proved by the defendant and the heba in question was not also be proved the learned Assistant Judge observed that the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree. Accordingly he declared that the heba bil ewaj is a fraudulent, collusive and inoperative document and the plaintiff-petitioner is not bound by aforesaid fraudulent heba-bil-ewaj. The learned Subordinate Judge on the other hand found that the plaintiff petitioner having admitted that the signature appearing in the heba is hers and further that the document being heba bil ewaj dated 26.10.72 and the suit was filed on 2.6.92 the suit is absolutely barred by limitation. He further observed that the plaintiff—having admitted her signature the plaintiff ought to have filed the suit within 6 years of the dale appearing in the document. Furthermore she was aware of the transaction as appearing in Ext. Kha as such she cannot challenge the same. The learned Subordinate Judge appear to have committed serious error of law as he considered the admission of the plaintiff that she put her LTI in the heba bil ewaj but he failed to consider the circumstances in which she had to put her signature and she disordered the heba bil ewaj by saying that fraud having been practised upon her and she did not know about the contents of the deed and she put her signature in good faith on the sale of 15 decimals of land and her signature was collusively used in the heba bil ewaj and furthers no exchange was proved or established. The learned judge committed serious error of law in not considering the circumstances as such his findings are not sustainable in law. Furthermore the plaintiff as the owner and having been in possession although challenged the heba bil ewaj as such burden is lying upon the defendant to prove that the heba is genuine. Lastly the learned Subordinate Judge did not discuss about the evidence of the witnesses and furthermore he did not controvert the findings of fact arrived at by the trial Court. In that view of the matter the judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, are liable to be set aside.
